I can't write them well, despite having been a member for months, and having spent a year reading SCPs before joining.

Just like eating a ton of gourmet meals does not make the eater a gourmet chef, reading a ton of SCPs does not automatically guarantee that the reader will be an excellent writer.

Have you read the corresponding discussion pages for successful SCP articles? Those can be really helpful, especially when the author provides an introductory post at the beginning explaining some of the creative process and how they put together the work.

You can also take a look at our Essays on Style, where some prolific site writers talk about how they approach writing for the SCP-verse: http://www.scp-wiki.net/essays-on-style

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Stereotypes:

  • Phantom - One day they just… vanished. Works may have been left undone, "I'm working on this" statements are common. No one has a real phone number or email address to contact them.
  • Spectre - Similar to the phantom, but occasionally their articles are modified slightly. Commets and mails are still not responded to.
  • Poltergeist - Similar to the Phantom, they seem to have disappeared from this reality… Unless someone modifies their article SLIGHTLY then the screaming ghost reappears from beyond with an unholy wail that will chill your soul!
  • Guru Meditation Error - Someone whose Wikidot "Karma" level has maxed out, so people assume he's staff (or that he has any clue about what he's talking about) when really what he's done was messed around in sandboxes.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
What amuses me about the proposed action is the excessively particular treatment this piece of work is getting compared to the four other non-serious essays.

In particular, I see no principial difference between this article and Eric_H's standard form of downvotes, as they are different takes on a single problem.

I thus propose the following. The section of "Humour essays" to be in entirety moved from the Guide Hub to the Joke SCPs page, where a good deal of non-SCP humour articles already dwell, thus it's both following sensible precedent, not orphaning the page , and treating it fairly with respect to other similar pages.

Bright then has actually gone the full way and say there's no harm to doing it, which, given he's unilaterally deleted pages he didn't like shouldn't surprise anyone.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If this is meant to be informative and helpful — which parts seem to imply — it fails.

The category it's in is aptly titled "Humour essays"
It's description states:

Author Stereotypes: A tongue-in-cheek list satirizing common noob stereotypes.

I think it's remarkably obvious it's meant to be funny.

If you have to put a warning on the top of the page that tells that they shouldn't do what you say in any way shape or form because your advice is actively malicious, then why do you have it here in the first place?

The advice is there so that comment threads wouldn't devolve into endless references to this article, which would very quickly cease to be funny. Mind you, this guide came about before the criticism policy in its current form - these days the warning might as well not be there.

It's not advice, it's not actively malicious, and last of all… many TV programmes have a "Do not try this at home" disclaimer, yet they are still aired.

If this is meant to be entertaining — which is the case — it also fails. The humour is dull, long-winded, and in general comes off as fairly mean-spirited. There's no punchline and no purpose.

It doesn't fail - you find it unfunny while over 80 people think the opposite, for a combined score of +75.
Feel free to downvote, but don't pretend your opinion is in any way an objective state of matters.

As a final word I would like to remark that these days, the content of this page is no less relevant than it was at the time of its writing, and that closing one's eyes before uncomfortable truths doesn't make them go away.
I am dismayed that there is a number of staff apparently eager to abuse their authority and circumvent the deletions process to remove a page that has been well received, having a rating well over the site average, while breaking no set site rules.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm going to disagree with you.

I've always felt there are three SCP-Wikis.

  1. There are the articles which are where the types of people you refer to can be shown.
  2. There are the forums, where the behaviors listed on this article are shown.
  3. There are the chat channels, which have their own special flavor of people.

Everyone here has at least a few of the traits listed, to a greater or lesser degree. Sometimes it's not a bad thing - lately one of my favorite phrases for newbies seems to be "That sounds like an interesting idea - YOU should write that up!" (It's amazing how many people think "I'll post what I want some else to write for me!")

Look, not all the things that list (except the reactions in forum) are bad. "Straight On Till Morning" and falls (in my opinion) directly into "The Non-Sequitur" Is that an issue? Well, no - it's well written and so are well received.

Many or the -J articles also fall into some of these, but - again, they're well written.

Truthfully, there are a LOT more stereotypes that aren't listed.

  • The Old Timer that whines for "the good old days"
  • The Yo-Yo who appears and disappears repeatedly.
  • The Non-author that speaks in a tone of authority.
  • The Loudmouth that people assume must be a mod/admin/someone in charge.

The thing is that we generally don't see the "other" in our self. Most people don't (won't, can't) realize that they do fall into one of these categories - that they have or are displaying negative behaviors.

This page isn't mean spirited, although it may be mocking. But it can only mock you if it's true. And if it's true, it's probably something that you need to work on. (Not you, Djoric - generic you.)

It's long agreed that this shouldn't be used as a "You're doing QQQ behaviour and Mac says you shouldn't!" any more than the "Generic SCP writeup form" was supposed to be. (Did that get deleted?)

We're not the "You better have a thick skin to post here!" that we used to be, but the fact is neither are we supposed to coddle people. This isn't where you go to for a participation prize. It's where you open a text editor and concentrate until your forehead bleeds and the blood forms words and if you're VERY lucky eventually the words make sense.

I feel this has a place here. Further, I feel there probably needs to be a "Harsh Advice Hub" that links things like this.

Anyway - my 2 Yen.
